title: How a block builds on other kinds
statement: How a lesson's separately made blocks can build on what blocks of other kinds taught, when each is made from the text, the question and its own kind alone.
detail: The 9 October audit of the lesson engine asked for the key-word deck to be seeded from the word web's key words when a lesson has both (`g9-transformer-audit/2026-10-09-best-of-everything.json`). The build that followed found that a block is made from the text, the question and its own kind only, and cannot see the rest of the lesson. So with a word web present, the key-word block is listed as skipped in the animated export and drawn only on the engine's plain screen (`g9-transformer-audit/2026-10-09-builders.json`). Only a later block of the same kind is told what earlier ones cover, and a block's key hashes just the maker and kind versions, the text, the question, the kind and its number (`g9/transformer/src/blocks.js`, lines 23-25 and 67-74). The engine's known gaps still say that key words are not seeded from the word web's words (`g9/transformer/README.md`, line 114).
against: A 3D version joins them after the fact: it puts the word web's key words into its own key-words step, as a deck labelled with the web's centre word (`g9/transformer/src/glue/threejs-render.js`, lines 219 and 224).

evidence.quote: KW is not seeded from the strip's word web, as the audit asked. A block is made from text, question and mechanic only and cannot see the strip.
If the strip has a word-web block, seed the deck from its keys.
